subject: Initial token latency: SSE vs WebSocket and cadence follow-up
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Siddharth Rao <sid@devops-ai.com>, Evan Lewis <evan@devops-ai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T15:02:00-04:00
Subject: Follow-up: TTFT & streaming cadence goals (recap + asks)

Thanks again for taking the time today — good discussion. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can size a pilot: 

High-level customer goals we captured on the call:
- Target the initial token (TTFT) to be < 120ms p95 for typical 16–32 token responses.
- End-to-end streaming cadence: chunks delivered ~100–200ms apart (prefer smaller frequent chunks vs one big chunk).
- Sustained throughput: 250 req/s with spikes to ~600 req/s for 20–60s promo bursts.
- Concurrency: ~60 simultaneous active requests during peak; want graceful tail behavior when concurrency hits 100+.

Please confirm the above numbers — especially the p95 TTFT threshold and your peak burst behavior — and attach any load profiles you already have.

Our asks / next steps from Redwood: 
1) Can you share a short sample traffic profile (CSV or JMeter) that includes request arrival distribution and typical prompt sizes?
2) If SSE is preferred, confirm whether you need a persistent connection per worker, or if a connection pool is acceptable (we usually recommend per-worker persistent SSE for lowest TTFT).
3) Confirm acceptable chunk cadence (you said ‘snappy and steady’ — if you have a concrete number that helps).
4) If you have strict cost constraints, flag that so we can propose Dedicated vs Hosted sizing.

I attached our lightweight performance checklist and a short SSE vs WebSocket matrix to help you map options. Laura (cc) will propose a technical pilot with explicit acceptance criteria once we get your traffic sample.

Thanks — I’ll hold Monday/Tuesday next week for a short pilot kickoff if that works.

— Ben

Subject: Re: Follow-up: TTFT & streaming cadence goals (recap + asks)

Thanks Ben — great summary. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

Confirmed targets (internal):
- TTFT: our product team wants p95 <= 120ms for short responses (10–40 tokens). p50 target < 40ms would be ideal.
- Streaming cadence: we prefer chunk cadence in the 125–200ms range; lower is OK as long as chunk size stays reasonable (we want progressive UX, not too many 1–2 token fragments).
- Throughput: baseline expected steady-state 250 rps; planned promo windows see spikes to ~600 rps for up to 60s.
- Concurrency: typical concurrency 45–60; worst-case observed 110 during stress tests.
- Average response length: ~180 tokens; however UI streams first few tokens immediately to show typing.

Attached a small sample: devopsai-load-sample.csv — it contains a 10-minute capture (arrival timestamps + prompt token sizes + user_id).

Two technical notes / asks for Redwood: 
1) We’d like to understand whether you recommend SSE or WebSocket for keeping TTFT low across many small clients. Our preference is SSE for simplicity but we can do WebSocket if it materially improves tail performance.
2) During bursts we care more about TTFT than long-run throughput cost; we’d accept some higher per-token cost during the 60s bursts if it guarantees ≤ 150ms TTFT p95.

Happy to hop on a short follow-up with Laura and Marcus to map the pilot specifics.

— Sid

Subject: Re: Follow-up: TTFT & streaming cadence goals (recap + asks)

Hi Sid / Ben — thanks for the sample and the clarity on targets. Quick technical readout and proposed acceptance criteria for the pilot: 

Quick readout from the sample (scoped):
- Your CSV shows median prompt tokens ~40, 95th prompt tokens ~420 (rare). Avg response token length ~180 as you said.
- Baseline arrival rate matches 250 rps steady with short bursts up to 580 rps in the 10-min capture.

Recommended configuration for the pilot (to meet TTFT targets):
1) Dedicated small pool (reserved) for the pilot: 2-4 GPU nodes (model-dependent) with autoscale threshold tuned for the promo bursts.
2) Disable cross-request batching for low TTFT in the pilot; enable prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts.
3) SSE as default transport: keep per-worker persistent SSE connections — avoids connection setup on every request. WebSocket acceptable if you need multiplexing across browser tabs.
4) Chunking parameters: aim for ~120–180ms cadence; target ~20–40 tokens per chunk (depending on tokenization). If UI requires earlier visual feedback, we can send a tiny initial delta (4–8 tokens) at ~60–80ms and then switch to 140–180ms cadence for main chunks.

Pilot acceptance criteria (pass/fail):
- TTFT: p50 < 50ms, p95 < 150ms, p99 < 300ms under steady-state 250 rps and concurrency 60.
- Streaming: average chunk interval between 100–200ms for >80% of streamed sessions.
- Throughput: system sustains 250 rps for 30 mins without queue growth; survives 600 rps burst for 60s with <= 10% increase in p95.

Test plan / timeline:
- Redwood will run a 2-hour technical pilot against a redwood-dedicated pool using your dev traffic (we’ll synthesize based on your CSV).
- We’ll run two passes: steady-state run (30–60m) and burst simulation (3–5 bursts of 60s each).
- Deliverables: latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for TTFT, per-chunk cadence histogram, and a small root-cause analysis for any missed SLOs.

Marcus and I will assemble the pilot config; suggested kickoff: Tue 2026-08-17 10:00 PT (we can shift if you need). I’ll prepare a brief runbook and share the DocuSign for a pilot agreement if needed.

— Laura
